fuzz and latexmk both exited 0 on the prior commit, but the operator
opened the PDF and found Z predicate text running off the right edge
and being cut off. Root cause: a newline in a schema predicate's LaTeX
source does not produce a line break -- only \\ does -- so several
multi-conjunct predicates that looked wrapped in the source typeset as
one very long line. Neither gate catches this: fuzz only checks that
the Z is well-typed, and latexmk only checks that pdflatex exits
cleanly, not whether content fits the page. The five affected schemas,
worst first, all in "alignment" overfulls (schemas render as
alignments, not paragraphs, so grepping only "in paragraph" missed
every one of them):

- VerifyCommandSignature: 468.5pt over (worst -- more than the full
  text width). Broke all eight cases at \land/\implies boundaries so
  each renders as its own visually distinct block, matching what the
  schema's exhaustiveness argument needs a reader to check by eye.
- ResolveCredential: 247.2pt over.
- ClassifyTrust: 177.8pt over.
- DaemonGate: 120.3pt over.
- the Basic Types given-set zed block: 38.4pt over.

All five now render fully within the page margin (verified by
rendering the affected pages to PNG and inspecting them directly, not
just by re-checking the log).

Also fixed two prose overfulls above the noise floor while in here:
the Package Map table's plain `l` column couldn't wrap long
descriptions (changed to p{10.5cm}, 51.1pt over -> 0), and an
unbreakable `filepath.EvalSymlinks`/`io.LimitReader` pair in Worker
Isolation (53.9pt over -> 0, via \allowbreak after the package-path
dot). The remaining 12 prose overfulls are all <=40pt, well inside the
72pt (1in) margin; spot-checked the two largest by rendering their
pages and confirmed nothing is visibly truncated.

fuzz -t docs/architecture.tex: exit 0, zero errors.
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error docs/architecture.tex: exit 0.
Overfull hbox count: 19 -> 12 (all "alignment"/Z overfulls eliminated;
0 of 5 remain, down from 5). Page count: 18 -> 20 (material, from the
five schemas now spanning more vertical lines each -- expected and
reported, not a regression).

Lesson for next time: fuzz proves the Z is well-typed and latexmk
proves the document compiles; neither checks whether the output fits
the page. Render affected pages to an image and look, don't infer
layout correctness from a clean exit code.
EOF
)"

tool_input.message:
Fixed, verified visually (not just by log), committed — not pushed. `b66cc3d` on `docs/daemon-status-artifact`.

**Corrected grep, before/after:**
- Before: 19 total overfulls (5 `alignment`/Z, 14 `paragraph`/prose).
- After: 12 total, **0 alignment/Z remaining**.

**The five Z schemas — all fixed by breaking at `\land`/`\implies`/`\iff` boundaries with `\\` + `\quad`:**
| schema | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `VerifyCommandSignature` | 468.5pt | 0 |
| `ResolveCredential` | 247.2pt | 0 |
| `ClassifyTrust` | 177.8pt | 0 |
| `DaemonGate` | 120.3pt | 0 |
| Basic Types given-set | 38.4pt | 0 |

Used exactly the `\quad`-continuation pattern you verified (confirmed `\t1` wasn't needed — didn't hit the tie-accent collision since I never tried it). For `VerifyCommandSignature` specifically, all eight cases now each read as their own block — I didn't just kill the overfull, I rendered the page to PNG and looked (page 16 of the built PDF): each case is now visually distinct and the exhaustiveness argument is checkable by eye, which was the actual point.

**Root cause, confirmed exactly as you diagnosed:** a bare newline inside a schema predicate is just whitespace to LaTeX; only `\\` breaks a line. Several multi-conjunct cases had 4-5 conjuncts concatenated onto one physical line because only some of the source's visual line breaks were real `\\`s.

**Two prose fixes beyond the Z, both above the noise floor:**
- Package Map table (51.1pt): plain `l` column couldn't wrap `internal/daemon/`'s long description. Changed to `p{10.5cm}`, matching the `p{6cm}` convention the MCP Tool Surface table already uses. → 0.
- Worker Isolation (53.9pt, the single worst remaining after the Z fixes): `filepath.EvalSymlinks` and `io.LimitReader` are unbreakable single tokens in `\texttt{}`. Added `\allowbreak` after each package-path dot (no visible hyphen, just a legal break point). → 0.

**Remaining 12 are all prose, all ≤40pt** — comfortably inside the 72pt (1in) margin, so still on the page. I didn't take that on faith: rendered the two worst (my own `Permission` paragraph at 39.9pt, and the `ChannelAssumption` paragraph at 38.0pt) to PNG and inspected both directly — nothing truncated, both pages read cleanly end to end. Stopped there rather than chasing single-digit-pt warnings with no visible effect; say the word if you want all 12 gone regardless.

**Verification:**
- `fuzz -t docs/architecture.tex` — exit 0, zero errors.
- `latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error docs/architecture.tex` — exit 0. (Hit one red herring on the way: a stale `.aux` from an earlier interrupted run threw `Extra }, or forgotten \endgroup` on a clean rebuild — `latexmk -c` hadn't removed it. Deleted `.aux`/`.log`/`.toc`/`.out` by hand and rebuilt from nothing; not a source defect, noted so it doesn't cost you time if you see it too.)
- Page count: 18 → 20. Material, expected, and worth flagging as you asked — the five schemas now span materially more vertical space each, not a sign of anything wrong.

Lesson taken for next time, stated in the commit message too: `fuzz` proves the Z well-typed, `latexmk` proves the document compiles, neither checks whether the output fits the page. That gap is exactly what let this ship. Rendering the affected pages and looking is now part of how I'll close out Z-heavy doc work going forward.
tool_input.summary: All 5 Z overflows fixed, verified by rendering pages; committed b66cc3d
